title: Build and choose a spam filter
brief: Fit naive Bayes and a kernel classifier, tune each with your own cross-validation, read a learning curve, and report a test score that selection never touched.
hints: In fit_nb, rows = X[y == k]; (rows.sum(axis=0) + alpha) divided by its own sum is one row of theta. Take the log after dividing, not before.
In cv_error, np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), held) gives the training rows. Build the folds once, outside the loop, so every setting is scored on the same folds.

In fit_krr_classifier, standardise with the training rows, build K = rbf_kernel(Z, Z, gamma), and solve for targets 2 * y - 1. predict_krr must standardise the queries with the same training mean and std.
In select_and_test, slice [:n_dev] for every selection step. The test rows [n_dev:] appear exactly once, in the final error_rate.
